title: TGLite: A Lightweight Programming Framework for Continuous-Time Temporal Graph Neural Networks
problem: Existing TGNN frameworks lack adequate support for continuous-time directed graphs (CTDGs) that represent topology changes as timestamped edge streams, and do not provide composability for exploring new model designs or facilitate CTDG-specific optimizations.
motivation: Continuous-time temporal graphs contain richer temporal information than discrete snapshots, making specialized programming abstractions essential for practitioners to explore and optimize CTDG-based TGNN models.
method: TGLite provides a lightweight programming framework with high-level abstractions for composing continuous-time temporal graph neural network models, supporting CTDG-specific optimizations and enabling practitioners to easily explore new architectural designs and optimizations for temporal graph learning tasks.
key_novelty: A programming framework specifically designed for continuous-time temporal graph neural networks with built-in support for CTDG-specific optimizations and model composability.
contributions: A lightweight programming framework tailored for continuous-time temporal GNNs
High-level abstractions enabling easy composition and exploration of CTDG models
Improved programmability compared to existing frameworks for temporal graph learning
limitations: Limitations and comparisons with specific baseline systems not discussed in abstract.
primary_theme: Programming framework for continuous-time temporal GNNs
